title: Close a 300 mm wafer shipping box in the maker's order: left edge in and latched, right side pressed flush and latched
instruction: Close the wafer shipping box. Carry its door by the two D-ring handles, set its left edge into the opening first and latch that side, then press the right side flush and latch it. Fold both D-rings down and let go.
context: 300 mm wafers, the substrate of every AI chip, travel from the wafer maker to the fab in front-opening shipping boxes (FOSBs), and fab and R&D staff re-pack them by hand (no count of how often is published). The box maker's manual for the SB300 gives the door's manual assembly: 'Grip the door and shipper box along the vertical edge (pivot edge) with one hand and rotate the door until the wafer cushion contacts the wafers. Latch the lock on the pivot edge first... Apply inward pressure to the opposite side of the door until it is flush to the shipper box opening and latch closed', and 'Make sure the door is properly seated before engaging the latches.' The cushion presses on 25 wafers, so the far side springs back out until it is held flush. While the first latch is turned the door is held only at its pivot edge, so the other hand must hold it. Tested: a set order, then a press held against a spring while the other hand latches.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) A 300 mm wafer shipping box in the size of the Entegris SB300 (385 wide, 333 deep, 337 tall, published), clear polycarbonate, about 7 kg (estimate), standing on a 2 cm printed plate (the maker's three-pin kinematic coupling is not modelled: the box is held by friction, 1.2). Its opening faces the robot: the rim's front face is at x = 34, centred at y = 0. The opening is 34 wide and 25 tall, centred 20.4 cm above the bench; the rim is 1.2 cm deep. It holds 25 wafers, 300 mm across and 0.775 mm thick, 10 mm apart, the first 44 mm above the box's floor (published pitch), their front edges 1.8 cm behind the rim's face. The wafers are fixed in the box's shape. (2) The door: clear polycarbonate, 363.7 wide and 258.0 tall (published), 2.5 cm thick and 1.0 kg (estimates). It stands on a printed rest (a 7.5 cm tall block with two 3.5 cm rails 2.8 cm apart) with its inner face at x = 28 and its centre 20.4 cm above the bench, centred at y = 0. On its inner face two spring pads, 2 x 2.5 cm, at y = +4.5 and -4.5, stand 3.3 cm proud and stand for the wafer cushion: each is a spring of 875 N/m, 14 N together at flush (estimate; the manual gives no force). (3) Two D-rings on the door's outer face at y = +15 and -15, mid-height: a 12 mm square bar, 5.2 cm long, on two 10 mm legs 4 cm apart, standing 3.6 cm proud of the face when lifted. They start lifted, with the bar upright. Each ring turns about its stem (a quarter turn, 90 degrees counter-clockwise seen from the robot latches it; the cam is set at 1 N m, an assumption within the manual's 4.4 N m maximum) and, after that, folds down onto the door. A latch counts as engaged only when its ring is turned 80 degrees or more while its side of the door is within 1 mm of flush on the box; an engaged latch holds its side to the rim with 12 N. Nothing else is on the bench. Run limit 3,000 steps (20 Hz). Real trial: a used SB300 or any 300 mm FOSB with its own door and cushion. In place of the wafers, 25 discs of 5052 aluminium, 300 mm across and 0.81 mm (0.032 in) thick, 154 g (a wafer is 128 g; the scene uses no wafer mass), edges filed round, one in each slot against the back stops: the diameter puts each front edge where a wafer's is, so the box's own cushion meets them and gives the real closing resistance; they sag about twice as much as silicon, under 1 mm at the front edge. They are cut four to a 610 mm sheet, seven sheets for about 156 USD, and reused. The top disc's front edge is marked red. Also the printed plate and rest, a pencil outline of the box on the plate, a phone above the box and a printed protractor on its top. Reset: unlatch both rings, lift them, set the door back on its rest. Entegris and SB300 are trademarks of Entegris, Inc., named for identification only.
scoring: Terms: a latch is engaged when its ring is turned 80 degrees or more while its side is within 1 mm of flush (real trial: the cam turns home only on a seated door). Tiers: 0.25 the left latch engaged. 0.5 both. 0.75 also the door flush all round: a 0.5 mm feeler enters at none of the four corners (the same feeler on the real box). 1.0 also both D-rings folded 80 degrees or more (real: flat on the door), the cushion pressed on the wafers (sim: both pads 6 mm or more; real: the door flush with all 25 discs in, the cushion seen on them through the clear door), and both grippers 3 cm clear and still for 1 s (real: video). Zeros that stick: the box moves more than 5 mm on its plate (real: the pencil outline) or lifts off it for 0.5 s; the door drops; the right latch engages before the left (real: the latch order on video); the cushion first touches the wafers with the door more than 5 degrees out of square (sim: 1 mm of pad travel; real: an overhead phone at 60 frames a second, the door's top edge read against a printed protractor centred on the pivot corner, in the first frame the cushion meets the red-marked top disc). No tier depends on the cushion's force or the cam's torque.
reset_notes: Both D-rings unlatched and lifted, the door on its rest at x = 28, the box on its plate. No seed changes the scene; the jitter run shifts free parts by up to 1 cm.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz on GPU, rigid parts and sprung joints. Wafers fixed in the box (real: seated in slots, held by the cushion). The cushion is two spring pads, 14 N at flush; it, the 1 kg door and the 1 N m cam torque are estimates, each with its real check in the README. A latch is a rule: it engages when its ring is turned while its side is within 1 mm of flush, then holds that side with 12 N. The demo reads the door's pose; a policy sees cameras. Meshes are hand-built from published sizes.
scores: demo: 1.0 on 3 of 3 README runs (560 of 3,000 steps), 4 of 4 jittered runs and one run on an RTX 5090; Dream-1 run: 0.0 (3,000 steps)
